services.name: Drain Cleaning
services.title: Drain Cleaning | Plumbing Solutions Austin | Austin, TX
services.meta: Plumbing Solutions Austin clears slow, blocked, and backing-up drains in Austin, TX. We inspect the line, locate the blockage, and clean the route.
services.blurb: We clear slow, blocked, gurgling, and backing-up drains across Austin.

paragraphs: A sink that gurgles, a shower that holds water, or a sewer odor near a floor drain usually points to a restriction in the drain line. Grease, soap residue, hair, wipes, and roots can narrow the pipe until water no longer moves freely.

We cover drain cleaning in Austin, Rollingwood, West Lake Hills, and Lost Creek. A single slow fixture can often be scheduled, but wastewater backing up, an overflowing toilet, or several drains stopping together should not wait because the blockage may be in a shared branch or sewer line.

sections.heading: Gurgling drains and sewer odor
paragraphs: Customers often report a kitchen sink that drains slowly, a bathtub that fills around their feet, or a washing machine drain that overflows. Other common signs include bubbles in a toilet bowl after the shower runs and a sewage smell coming from a floor drain.

A clog close to the fixture can act much like a blockage farther down the branch line. A dry trap can also create an odor without a solid blockage. We inspect the pipe and fixture because these symptoms can look alike from the room, yet each fault needs different work and can involve different materials and access.

sections.heading: Drain inspection and cable callout
paragraphs: We start the callout by checking which fixture is affected and whether nearby drains change when water runs. We test the drain flow, inspect the trap where accessible, and check cleanout openings before selecting a cable or other cleaning method.

Most household drain branches range from 1 1/2 to 4 inches in diameter. A fixture-level check and clearing can often be completed during the same visit. We may recommend a camera inspection or schedule further work if the blockage sits beyond the available cleanout, the line has root intrusion, or the pipe needs repair.

sections.heading: Pipe access and blockage depth
paragraphs: The route to the blockage affects the work. A cleanout near the exterior wall gives us a different path than a line reached through a cabinet, crawlspace, or roof vent. A clog near the trap generally takes less setup than debris farther along a branch or sewer line.

Pipe material and condition also matter. Older cast iron can hold scale inside the pipe, while a damaged clay or plastic line may need a camera inspection after cleaning. Roots, a seized cleanout cap, restricted access, and a line that requires property or municipal sign-off can add steps before the drain is fully cleared.

sections.heading: Fixture location and cleanout access
paragraphs: Tell us which room has the slow or backing-up fixture, such as the kitchen sink, shower, laundry standpipe, or floor drain. Let us know whether one drain is affected or whether water appears in a different fixture when another one runs.

If you can see a cleanout cap, tell us where it is located: outside, in a utility room, under a sink, or in a crawlspace. Keep cabinets, floor drains, and access panels clear where possible. Mention any recent grease, wipes, food scraps, or construction debris that may have entered the line. Call Plumbing Solutions Austin at (737) 300-9206 before a slow drain becomes standing wastewater or a sewer backup.

services.name: Water Heater Repair
services.h1: Water Heater Repair in Austin, TX
services.title: Water Heater Repair | Plumbing Solutions Austin, TX
services.meta: Plumbing Solutions Austin repairs water heaters in Austin, TX. We diagnose cold water, tank leaks, pilot faults, valves, and heating elements for homes.
services.blurb: Water heater fault checks for cold water, tank leaks, pilots, and relief valves.

paragraphs: A cold shower and a puddle beside the water heater often get called the same problem. From the hallway, a dry utility room with cold taps points toward the heating side; water on the floor points to a tank, valve, or supply connection.
We handle both faults at Plumbing Solutions Austin. We inspect gas and electric units, storage tanks, shutoff valves, relief valves, and the hot-water lines leaving the heater.

No hot water can sometimes wait if the tank is dry and there is no gas smell. A leaking tank, active discharge from the relief pipe, or a gas odor should not wait because water can damage flooring and a fuel fault needs isolation.

sections.heading: No hot water or tank leak
paragraphs: People report no hot water at any faucet, a shower that goes cold halfway through, or a pilot that will not stay lit. Others find water under the tank, a steady drip from the relief-valve pipe, or popping sounds during a heating cycle.

Cold water at every fixture can trace to a failed element, thermostat, burner, gas control, or power supply. A drip may come from a relief valve, a connection, or the tank itself, so similar reports can require different parts and labor after inspection.

sections.heading: Tank inspection and test
paragraphs: We start at the tank and trace the water, gas, or electrical path. We check the shutoff, thermostat setting, pilot or ignition system, burner or elements, venting, relief valve, drain valve, and visible fittings.

We test supply voltage on electric units or gas delivery and combustion components on gas units. We also measure incoming water pressure, which is commonly maintained within 40 to 80 psi in a residential plumbing system.

A diagnostic inspection commonly takes 30 to 60 minutes. We can often replace accessible elements, thermostats, ignition parts, relief valves, or flex connections on the same visit; tank replacement, vent changes, ordered parts, and permit work are booked separately.

sections.heading: Tank age, shutoff, access
paragraphs: The tank age and failed component affect the scope of work. An accessible thermostat or relief valve is different from a corroded tank fitting, and a shutoff valve that will not close adds isolation work before a part can be changed.

A utility closet, attic platform, or tight drain-pan opening can add removal and installation work. An ordered gas control, a replacement tank, or changes needing city sign-off require separate planning and may involve another visit.

sections.heading: Model plate and closet access
paragraphs: Find the model and serial number on the rating plate, usually attached to the side of the tank. Note the approximate installation age and whether the unit uses gas, electricity, or a heat-pump system.

Tell us which room holds the tank and whether hot water is missing at every faucet or only one shower. Let us know if the tank, relief-valve discharge pipe, or floor is wet, and whether the shutoff and electrical panel are accessible.
Call Plumbing Solutions Austin at (737) 300-9206; a tank leak can spread into flooring, drywall, and framing while it waits.

services.name: Toilet Repair
services.title: Toilet Repair | Plumbing Solutions Austin | Austin, TX
services.meta: Plumbing Solutions Austin handles running, leaking, rocking, and weak-flushing toilets in Austin, TX, with tank, valve, seal, and flange checks.
services.blurb: We repair running, leaking, rocking, and weak-flushing toilets in Austin.

paragraphs: A toilet that refills every few minutes can send water through the overflow tube for days. We often find a worn flapper, a failing fill valve, or a lift chain that no longer seals the flush valve correctly.
A slow leak beneath the toilet base can stain flooring, soften a subfloor, and loosen the closet bolts. A weak flush can also leave waste in the bowl, leading to repeated flushing and clogs.

We treat water at the base, continuous running, and a toilet that will not flush as work that should not wait. A sticking handle may wait briefly if the tank is not leaking, but a failed seal can waste water or damage the bathroom floor.

sections.heading: Toilet keeps running
paragraphs: We hear that the toilet keeps running, the tank makes a hissing sound, the handle does nothing, or the bowl will not clear. A tank that refills on its own may have a leaking flapper, a fill valve that will not shut off, or water reaching the overflow tube.

We also check toilets that rock on the floor, have water around the base, smell musty near the bowl, or leave a low water level after flushing. These symptoms can overlap, but we trace them to separate parts and repair costs after inspecting the tank, bowl, and floor connection.

sections.heading: Tank and bowl inspection
paragraphs: We start at the tank lid, flush handle, fill valve, flapper, overflow tube, and supply connection. We watch the flush cycle, check the bowl refill level, and test the shutoff valve before disturbing older fittings.

We check supply pressure, which normally falls between 40 and 80 psi in a residential plumbing system. A straightforward tank inspection often takes 20 to 40 minutes, and a dye test can show flapper seepage within 10 to 15 minutes.

We can complete a standard flapper, fill valve, lift chain, handle, or supply tube repair on the visit when the correct part is available and the shutoff operates. A damaged closet flange, soft subfloor, seized shutoff, or special-order flush valve may require further work or a return visit.

sections.heading: Fill valve, flange, and shutoff
paragraphs: Repair scope changes with the failed part. A worn flapper or loose lift chain is usually contained inside the tank, while an aging fill valve, cracked flush valve, or corroded closet bolt can involve more disassembly.
Access changes the work as well. A toilet set over tile, a concealed flange, or a shutoff valve that has seized can require careful removal and replacement of connected parts.

We also account for a manufacturer-specific valve or tank component that has to be ordered. If a property manager, building rule, or required sign-off affects access to the bathroom plumbing, we include that before work begins.

sections.heading: Tank model and bowl
paragraphs: Before calling, check whether the toilet is running now, leaking at the base, or failing to flush. Tell us which bathroom has the problem and whether the bowl rocks when you sit or press near the rim.

Look for the model number inside the tank or beneath the tank lid if it is printed there. Let us know the approximate age of the toilet, whether the shutoff valve turns, and whether the tank area is clear for access.
Call Plumbing Solutions Austin at (737) 300-9206 before a base leak soaks more of the flooring or a running tank sends more water into the overflow tube.

services.name: Pipe Leak Repair
services.h1: Pipe Leak Repair in Austin, TX
services.title: Pipe Leak Repair | Plumbing Solutions Austin | Austin, TX
services.meta: Plumbing Solutions Austin repairs leaking pipes in Austin, TX. We trace wet walls, hissing lines, ceiling stains, and failed valves before water spreads.
services.blurb: We trace and repair leaking pipes, valves, and hidden water lines.

paragraphs: A towel, bowl, or bucket under a drip is a sensible first move. It catches water and gives you time to find the shutoff valve. Tape around a small joint leak can also slow the drip for a short time.

A pipe leak usually keeps moving behind the cabinet, wall, or ceiling after the container fills. Water can follow framing, insulation, and electrical openings far from the visible stain. Pipe leak repair should not wait because a small supply-line leak can soak drywall and framing before the source is clear.

sections.heading: Water stains and hissing
paragraphs: Customers often call about a hissing sound inside a wall, a brown spot on the ceiling, or water collecting beneath a sink cabinet. A damp patch that grows after nobody has used the fixture can point to a pressurized pipe rather than a spill.

Other calls start with a water meter that keeps moving, a warm area of floor, or peeling paint near a baseboard. A wet ceiling can come from a fitting above it, while a hissing line may be hidden in a wall cavity. These signs can look alike from the room, but each leak has its own source, access work, and repair scope.

sections.heading: Leak inspection and pressure test
paragraphs: We start the callout by checking the visible pipe, shutoff valve, fixture connections, cabinet floor, and nearby wall surfaces. A visible-source inspection often takes 30 to 60 minutes. We use a moisture meter and pressure gauge to narrow down the route, with residential water pressure commonly set between 40 and 80 psi.

We can usually replace an exposed supply line, fitting, valve, or section of accessible copper, PEX, or PVC during the same visit. We isolate the water line before removing a failed connection and test the repair afterward. A leak behind tile, under a slab, or inside a finished wall may need a separate visit for access, pipe replacement, and surface restoration.

sections.heading: Pipe access and seized shutoffs
paragraphs: An exposed pipe below a cabinet takes less access work than a line behind drywall, tile, or a ceiling. A shutoff valve that will not close can expand the work because the water must be isolated elsewhere before the damaged fitting comes apart.

Pipe material also affects the repair. Aging galvanized pipe may reveal weak threads beside the first leak, while copper, PEX, and PVC use different fittings and connection methods. A special valve or fitting may need to be ordered, and work that requires inspection or sign-off can add steps beyond the leak itself.

sections.heading: Pipe material and access panel
paragraphs: Tell us which room has the leak and which fixture or appliance the pipe serves. Note whether water is running now, whether the stain is on a ceiling or wall, and whether you can reach the pipe through a cabinet, crawlspace, or access panel.

If the pipe feeds an appliance, find the model number on its manufacturer plate. A photo of the shutoff valve, fitting, and damaged area can help identify the pipe material before we arrive. Call Plumbing Solutions Austin at (737) 300-9206 before water keeps spreading through drywall, insulation, or wood framing.

services.name: Faucet Repair
services.title: Faucet Repair | Plumbing Solutions Austin | Austin, TX
services.meta: Plumbing Solutions Austin repairs dripping, loose, and low-flow faucets in Austin, TX. We inspect cartridges, valves, handles, and under-sink connections.
services.blurb: We repair dripping, loose, noisy, and low-flow faucets across Austin.

paragraphs: People call us because “the faucet will not stop dripping,” “the handle is loose,” or “hardly any water comes out.” Those words point to parts inside the faucet body, such as a cartridge, stem, seal, aerator, or mounting nut.
We also hear about a squeal at the sink, water around the base, and a handle that turns without changing the flow. We inspect the fixture rather than assuming every drip needs the same replacement.

A slow drip may wait briefly if the faucet shuts off and the cabinet stays dry. Water running from the spout, pooling beneath the sink, or soaking the vanity should not wait because it can damage the cabinet, flooring, and supply connections.

sections.heading: Dripping faucet and loose handle
paragraphs: A faucet that drips after the handle is shut off can have a worn cartridge, damaged washer, or scored valve seat. A handle that feels loose, spins, or comes off may need a screw, adapter, stem, or handle assembly.

Low flow from one faucet often starts at a clogged aerator, especially if other fixtures have normal flow. A grinding, squealing, or clicking sound can come from the cartridge or a restricted internal passage.

Water appearing at the base of the faucet may come from worn seals, a loose mounting nut, or a connection under the sink. These symptoms can look similar from the counter, but each fault involves different parts and a different repair scope.

sections.heading: Sink fixture inspection
paragraphs: We start at the sink fixture and check the handle movement, spout flow, aerator, cartridge area, and water around the base. Under the cabinet, we inspect the shutoff valves, supply hoses, mounting hardware, and drain opening for signs that water has traveled below the countertop.

We can test water pressure at the fixture when flow points to a supply issue. Typical residential pressure is often kept between 40 and 80 psi, though a clogged aerator can reduce flow even with normal pressure in the line.

An aerator, handle screw, seal, cartridge, or supply connector can often be replaced during the same visit when the matching part is available. A specialty cartridge, discontinued finish part, seized shutoff valve, or corroded faucet mount may require a return visit after the correct component is ordered.

sections.heading: Cartridges, shutoffs, and access
paragraphs: The part inside the faucet matters. A common cartridge or aerator is usually simpler to address than a brand-specific valve assembly, a discontinued handle, or a finish-matched component that must be ordered.

Access beneath the sink also changes the work. An open cabinet with working shutoff valves allows the faucet to be isolated and removed more directly than a crowded vanity, a seized valve, or corroded hardware behind the basin.

The simpler end of the repair is an accessible fixture with an identifiable replacement part. The work becomes more involved when a shutoff will not close, the faucet is tightly corroded to the countertop, or a building manager must approve water shutdown or access.

sections.heading: Brand mark and room
paragraphs: Before you call, check which room has the faucet problem and whether it is a kitchen, bathroom, bar, laundry, or outdoor fixture. Note whether the faucet is dripping from the spout, leaking at the base, or running inside the cabinet.
Look for a brand mark on the handle, spout, or escutcheon plate. A model code may also appear in the installation booklet, receipt, product box, or on a label beneath the sink.

Tell us the approximate age of the fixture, whether either shutoff valve works, and how much room is available under the cabinet. Photos of the faucet and the connections can help identify the cartridge and mounting style.
Call Plumbing Solutions Austin at (737) 300-9206 if water is collecting around the faucet base or cabinet floor, since that moisture can swell wood and damage the sink cabinet.

services.name: Garbage Disposal Repair
services.h1: Garbage Disposal Repair in Austin, TX
services.title: Disposal Repair | Plumbing Solutions Austin | Austin, TX
services.meta: Plumbing Solutions Austin handles garbage disposal repair in Austin, TX, for humming motors, sink leaks, jams, odors, and units that will not start.
services.blurb: Repair for humming, leaking, jammed, or foul-smelling garbage disposals.

paragraphs: Older kitchens across Austin, Rollingwood, West Lake Hills, and Lost Creek often have original sink flanges, switches, and disposal mounts. Those fittings can loosen or corrode as the disposal motor and drain connections age inside the sink cabinet.

We repair units that jam after food waste, stop at the wall switch, leak around the mounting ring, or make a low humming sound. A humming, leaking, or non-starting disposal should not be left in use because a stalled motor can burn out and water under the sink can damage the cabinet base.

sections.heading: Humming motor and sink odor
paragraphs: Customers often tell us the disposal hums but will not grind, makes a grinding or rattling noise, or trips off after the switch is turned on. Others report water dripping from the bottom of the unit, a leak at the sink flange, or standing water on the disposal side of the sink.

A sour sink odor can come from food trapped around the splash guard, but it can also point to residue inside the grinding chamber. A disposal that will not turn on may have a reset issue, a switch problem, a wiring fault, or a failed motor. These symptoms can sound alike from the kitchen, yet the motor, mounting ring, drain connection, and electrical parts lead to different repair work.

sections.heading: Under-sink inspection
paragraphs: We inspect the disposal body, mounting assembly, sink flange, discharge tube, dishwasher connection, switch, and wiring under the cabinet. We test the reset button and use a meter to check the electrical supply before we decide whether the fault is mechanical or electrical.

A basic inspection and operational test typically takes 20 to 40 minutes. We can often clear an accessible jam, reset an overload, tighten a fitting, or replace an available splash guard or mounting part on the same visit. A failed motor, damaged mounting assembly, or unit requiring a matching replacement part may need a return visit after the part is obtained.

sections.heading: Motor age and cabinet access
paragraphs: The disposal motor and its age affect the scope of repair. An older unit with a worn grinding chamber, leaking lower seal, or damaged mounting ring may need more than a reset or adjustment. A model that uses a specific switch, stopper, or mounting component can also require an ordered part.

Cabinet access matters around the drain trap, dishwasher hose, electrical cord, and water shutoff. Tight shelving, a seized shutoff, corroded fasteners, or a disposal installed behind fixed plumbing adds work before the unit can be removed or reconnected. We assess those fittings at the sink so the repair matches the actual fault and access.

sections.heading: Model plate and sink cabinet
paragraphs: Check the model number on the label underneath or on the side of the disposal body if the label is visible. Tell us which kitchen sink has the issue and whether the unit hums, leaks, grinds, or does nothing at the switch.

Let us know whether water is running from the disposal, the sink flange, or the drain connection. Clear anything stored in front of the sink cabinet if access is limited by bins, shelves, or cleaning supplies.
Call Plumbing Solutions Austin at (737) 300-9206 with the model number and symptoms. A leak at the disposal flange can swell the cabinet floor, and repeated switching can worsen a stalled motor.

home.title: Plumbing in Austin, TX | Plumbing Solutions Austin
home.meta: Call Plumbing Solutions Austin for plumbing repairs and drain work in Austin, TX. We discuss the problem at your sink, toilet, or pipe before a visit.
home.firstBreak: We are ready to hear what is happening.
home.secondBreak: Let us start with the fixture or room.
about: We hear about drains gurgling in kitchens, water pooling beside toilets, and pipes dripping beneath sinks. We also find sewer odor in bathrooms, low flow at faucets, and damp patches on ceilings.

We may start a plumbing job beneath a sink or behind a bathroom wall. The cause is often a worn connection or blocked pipe, and we repair the affected part. We cover Austin, Rollingwood, West Lake Hills, and Lost Creek.
For a water heater, we may repair a limited fault in a replaceable part. We may recommend replacement if the tank has a leak or corrosion. We tell you which before any price is discussed.
